1	# MoS2: expert Raman notes
2	
3	Scope: 2H-MoS2 (and the 3R polytype where noted). Numbers appear only where they were read in the cited source;
4	the locator says where. "Consensus" means several independent sources agree; "single source" means one paper.
5	Positions move 1 to 3 cm-1 with calibration, substrate, strain and doping: reason from differences and trends.
6	
7	## Signature and irreps
8	- Bulk 2H (D6h): Raman-active A1g, E1g, E2g (two); E1g is forbidden in backscattering from the basal plane
9	  (Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.3 and p.6).
10	- Monolayer (D3h): E2g1 becomes E', A1g becomes A1'; odd N is D3h, even N is D3d, so labels change with parity
11	  (Zhang X. 2015, p.3, p.7).
12	- Main lines at 514.5 nm on 285 nm SiO2/Si: 1L E' 384.0, A1' 403.1 cm-1 (separation 19.1); bulk 382.2 / 407.4
13	  (25.2) (Lee C. et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b). Consensus.
14	- Widths: E2g1 about 2.1 cm-1; A1g 3 to 6 cm-1, broadening from 6L to 2L (Lee 2010, p.4).
15	- Bulk interlayer shear mode E2g2 near 32 cm-1 (Zhang X. 2015, p.11).
16	
17	## Thickness
18	- E2g1 softens and A1g stiffens with N; the separation is the standard layer counter up to about 4L
19	  (Lee 2010, Fig. 2b). It holds on SiO2, hBN, mica, Gel-Film, Au and few-layer graphene (Buscema M. et al. 2014,
20	  arXiv:1311.3869, p.4). Consensus.
21	- Above about 5L the separation saturates; use the low-frequency shear (C) and layer-breathing (LB) modes, whose
22	  positions follow a linear-chain model with different branches for odd and even N
23	  (Zhang X. et al. 2013, PRB 87, 115413, arXiv:1212.6796, abstract and Fig. 2; review Fig. 5, p.8).
24	- Stacking: 2H vs 3R bilayers differ in the low-frequency modes, not in the E/A pair
25	  (Ranjuna M. K. et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13, 16418, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-43756-w, p.2, Fig. 1d to f).
26	- Intensity is not a thickness measure on its own: MoS2 and Si intensities oscillate with N through optical
27	  interference; the Si-normalized MoS2 signal is monotonic and can be used (Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835,
28	  abstract; companion of ACS Nano 6, 7381, 2012).
29	
30	## Strain and doping
31	- Uniaxial tensile strain: E' softens about -4.5 cm-1/% (1L) and splits into E'+ and E'-; A1' shows no
32	  measurable shift (Conley H. J. et al. 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626, arXiv:1305.3880, text). Consensus.
33	- Electron doping (electrolyte gate): 1L A1g softens about 4 cm-1 and broadens about 6 cm-1 at 1.8e13 cm-2;
34	  E2g1 moves about 0.6 cm-1 (Chakraborty B. et al. 2012, PRB 85, 161403, arXiv:1206.1758, text).
35	- Rule of thumb: A1' shift with broadening points to doping; E' shift, especially with splitting, to strain.
36	- Substrate doping: A1g of 1L stiffens by up to about 2 cm-1 from SiO2 (lowest) to hBN (highest) while E2g1
37	  barely moves, attributed to lower electron density on hBN (Buscema 2014, p.7, Fig. 4c).
38	- Transfer can shift peaks through strain release and interface effects (Zhang X. et al. 2025, Nat. Commun. 16,
39	  4468, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-59803-1, p.4); monolayer separation is "typically about 20 cm-1" there.
40	
41	## Defects and quality
42	- LA(M) near 227 cm-1 is the main defect-activated band; I(LA)/I(first order) scales with defect density
43	  (Mignuzzi S. et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411, abstract). Quantitative L_D calibration not verified here.
44	- Few-layer modes near 286 and 471 cm-1 (forbidden for 1L backscattering) are intrinsic resonant modes, not
45	  defects; strongest at UV excitation such as 3.8 eV (Scheuschner N. et al. 2015, PRB 91, 235409,
46	  arXiv:1503.08980, pp.8 to 9).
47	- Sulfur vacancies show up more in widths and relative intensities than in positions at high temperature
48	  (Ranjuna 2023, p.9). Narrow lines (E2g1 about 2 cm-1, Lee 2010) indicate good crystals.
49	
50	## Temperature and heating
51	- Both main modes redshift on heating. First-order coefficients: few-layer -1.32e-2 (E2g1) and -1.23e-2 (A1g)
52	  cm-1/K (Sahoo S. et al. 2013, J. Phys. Chem. C, doi:10.1021/jp402509w, arXiv:1302.5865, p.6); 1L
53	  -0.013 (E2g) and -0.016 (A1g) cm-1/K (Lanzillo N. et al. 2013, APL, doi:10.1063/1.4819337, Table I);
54	  1L on SiO2 is nonlinear below room temperature, literature values -0.011 to -0.017 cm-1/K
55	  (Taube A. et al. 2014, ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, Table 1, p.5). Consensus on sign and order; values
56	  scatter with substrate and sample.
57	- Laser heating redshifts and broadens both modes (Ranjuna 2023, pp.5 to 6, Fig. 6). On a suspended few-layer
58	  flake A1g shifts about 5.4 cm-1/mW (Sahoo 2013, p.10): suspended flakes heat strongly.
59	- Damage: 10 mW at 514 nm, scanned, sublimates upper layers of multilayer MoS2 on SiO2 and leaves a monolayer,
60	  because the bottom layer is heat-sunk to the substrate (Castellanos-Gomez A. et al. 2012, Nano Lett. 12, 3187,
61	  arXiv:1206.4323, p.3).
62	- Modest laser exposure in air can also increase Raman intensity 3 to 5 times, harden A1g by 1.4 cm-1 and soften
63	  E2g1 by 1 cm-1 (attributed to defect healing) (Bera A. et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386, abstract). So repeated
64	  scans of one spot are not independent.
65	
66	## Excitation wavelength and resonance
67	- 633 nm (near the A exciton) gives resonant spectra rich in second-order bands that evolve with N: 2LA(M)
68	  near 450, A1g(M)-LA(M) near 179, a B1u Davydov partner of A1g near 403 that grows with N, and a 420 cm-1
69	  band (B2g2+E1u-type combination) that is absent in 1L (Zhang X. 2015, Fig. 12, pp.13 to 14; 1L assignments
70	  in Table III, p.15). Off resonance (514, 532 nm) the
71	  spectrum is mainly E' and A1'.
72	- UV (325 nm) enhances combination modes 750 to 840 cm-1 (Zhang X. 2015, p.15).
73	- Consequence: peak lists and intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line.
74	
75	## Polarization and substrate
76	- Backscattering, linear: A1g/A1' appears in XX and vanishes in YX; E2g1/E' is present in both with equal
77	  intensity (Zhang X. 2015, p.6 to 7, Fig. 3c). Use this to separate overlapping modes.
78	- Substrate also modulates intensity through interference (Buscema 2014, abstract; Li arXiv:1308.3835).
79	- Mica has a Bg mode that can overlap A1g (Buscema 2014, p.7).
80	
81	## Pitfalls and artifacts
82	- Spectral resolution: Lee 2010 used 2.7 cm-1; the 1L-2L separation step is about 2 cm-1, comparable.
83	- 3R and 1T polytypes break the 2H rules (see materials.md); check stacking before applying the separation.
84	- Calibrate with Si (about 520 cm-1) in the same spectrum; report the laser line.
85	- Doping and strain both move A1': a single spectrum cannot separate all causes; say so.
86	
87	## What to ask
88	- Laser wavelength, power at the sample, spot size, objective; was power varied?
89	- Substrate (SiO2 thickness), suspended or supported, encapsulated (hBN), transferred or as-grown.
90	- Exfoliated or CVD; age and storage; any gating or illumination history.
91	- Polarization configuration; temperature and environment (air, vacuum).
92	- Grating, resolution and calibration reference.
93	
94	## Reference figures
95	- Lee 2010, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2a,b: spectra and E2g1/A1g positions vs layer number (514.5 nm).
96	- Zhang X. 2013, arXiv:1212.6796, Fig. 2: 5L, 6L, bulk spectra incl. low-frequency modes, XX vs YX.
97	- Zhang X. 2015, arXiv:1502.00701, Fig. 12: resonant (633 nm) spectra of 1, 2, 4, 7L and bulk.
98	- Conley 2013, arXiv:1305.3880, Fig. 2: E' splitting under uniaxial strain.

- Bulk 2H (D6h): Raman-active A1g, E1g, E2g (two); E1g is forbidden in backscattering from the basal plane
  (Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.3 and p.6).
- Monolayer (D3h): E2g1 becomes E', A1g becomes A1'; odd N is D3h, even N is D3d, so labels change with parity
  (Zhang X. 2015, p.3, p.7).
- Main lines at 514.5 nm on 285 nm SiO2/Si: 1L E' 384.0, A1' 403.1 cm-1 (separation 19.1); bulk 382.2 / 407.4
  (25.2) (Lee C. et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b). Consensus.
- Widths: E2g1 about 2.1 cm-1; A1g 3 to 6 cm-1, broadening from 6L to 2L (Lee 2010, p.4).
- Bulk interlayer shear mode E2g2 near 32 cm-1 (Zhang X. 2015, p.11).

## Thickness
- E2g1 softens and A1g stiffens with N; the separation is the standard layer counter up to about 4L
  (Lee 2010, Fig. 2b). It holds on SiO2, hBN, mica, Gel-Film, Au and few-layer graphene (Buscema M. et al. 2014,
  arXiv:1311.3869, p.4). Consensus.
- Above about 5L the separation saturates; use the low-frequency shear (C) and layer-breathing (LB) modes, whose
  positions follow a linear-chain model with different branches for odd and even N
  (Zhang X. et al. 2013, PRB 87, 115413, arXiv:1212.6796, abstract and Fig. 2; review Fig. 5, p.8).
- Stacking: 2H vs 3R bilayers differ in the low-frequency modes, not in the E/A pair
  (Ranjuna M. K. et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13, 16418, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-43756-w, p.2, Fig. 1d to f).
- Intensity is not a thickness measure on its own: MoS2 and Si intensities oscillate with N through optical
  interference; the Si-normalized MoS2 signal is monotonic and can be used (Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835,
  abstract; companion of ACS Nano 6, 7381, 2012).

## Strain and doping
- Uniaxial tensile strain: E' softens about -4.5 cm-1/% (1L) and splits into E'+ and E'-; A1' shows no
  measurable shift (Conley H. J. et al. 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626, arXiv:1305.3880, text). Consensus.
- Electron doping (electrolyte gate): 1L A1g softens about 4 cm-1 and broadens about 6 cm-1 at 1.8e13 cm-2;
  E2g1 moves about 0.6 cm-1 (Chakraborty B. et al. 2012, PRB 85, 161403, arXiv:1206.1758, text).
- Rule of thumb: A1' shift with broadening points to doping; E' shift, especially with splitting, to strain.
- Substrate doping: A1g of 1L stiffens by up to about 2 cm-1 from SiO2 (lowest) to hBN (highest) while E2g1
  barely moves, attributed to lower electron density on hBN (Buscema 2014, p.7, Fig. 4c).
- Transfer can shift peaks through strain release and interface effects (Zhang X. et al. 2025, Nat. Commun. 16,
  4468, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-59803-1, p.4); monolayer separation is "typically about 20 cm-1" there.

## Defects and quality
- LA(M) near 227 cm-1 is the main defect-activated band; I(LA)/I(first order) scales with defect density
  (Mignuzzi S. et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411, abstract). Quantitative L_D calibration not verified here.
- Few-layer modes near 286 and 471 cm-1 (forbidden for 1L backscattering) are intrinsic resonant modes, not
  defects; strongest at UV excitation such as 3.8 eV (Scheuschner N. et al. 2015, PRB 91, 235409,
  arXiv:1503.08980, pp.8 to 9).
- Sulfur vacancies show up more in widths and relative intensities than in positions at high temperature
  (Ranjuna 2023, p.9). Narrow lines (E2g1 about 2 cm-1, Lee 2010) indicate good crystals.

## Temperature and heating
- Both main modes redshift on heating. First-order coefficients: few-layer -1.32e-2 (E2g1) and -1.23e-2 (A1g)
  cm-1/K (Sahoo S. et al. 2013, J. Phys. Chem. C, doi:10.1021/jp402509w, arXiv:1302.5865, p.6); 1L
  -0.013 (E2g) and -0.016 (A1g) cm-1/K (Lanzillo N. et al. 2013, APL, doi:10.1063/1.4819337, Table I);
  1L on SiO2 is nonlinear below room temperature, literature values -0.011 to -0.017 cm-1/K
  (Taube A. et al. 2014, ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, Table 1, p.5). Consensus on sign and order; values
  scatter with substrate and sample.
- Laser heating redshifts and broadens both modes (Ranjuna 2023, pp.5 to 6, Fig. 6). On a suspended few-layer
  flake A1g shifts about 5.4 cm-1/mW (Sahoo 2013, p.10): suspended flakes heat strongly.
- Damage: 10 mW at 514 nm, scanned, sublimates upper layers of multilayer MoS2 on SiO2 and leaves a monolayer,
  because the bottom layer is heat-sunk to the substrate (Castellanos-Gomez A. et al. 2012, Nano Lett. 12, 3187,
  arXiv:1206.4323, p.3).
- Modest laser exposure in air can also increase Raman intensity 3 to 5 times, harden A1g by 1.4 cm-1 and soften
  E2g1 by 1 cm-1 (attributed to defect healing) (Bera A. et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386, abstract). So repeated
  scans of one spot are not independent.

## Excitation wavelength and resonance
- 633 nm (near the A exciton) gives resonant spectra rich in second-order bands that evolve with N: 2LA(M)
  near 450, A1g(M)-LA(M) near 179, a B1u Davydov partner of A1g near 403 that grows with N, and a 420 cm-1
  band (B2g2+E1u-type combination) that is absent in 1L (Zhang X. 2015, Fig. 12, pp.13 to 14; 1L assignments
  in Table III, p.15). Off resonance (514, 532 nm) the
  spectrum is mainly E' and A1'.
- UV (325 nm) enhances combination modes 750 to 840 cm-1 (Zhang X. 2015, p.15).
- Consequence: peak lists and intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line.

## Polarization and substrate
- Backscattering, linear: A1g/A1' appears in XX and vanishes in YX; E2g1/E' is present in both with equal
  intensity (Zhang X. 2015, p.6 to 7, Fig. 3c). Use this to separate overlapping modes.
- Substrate also modulates intensity through interference (Buscema 2014, abstract; Li arXiv:1308.3835).
- Mica has a Bg mode that can overlap A1g (Buscema 2014, p.7).

## Pitfalls and artifacts
- Spectral resolution: Lee 2010 used 2.7 cm-1; the 1L-2L separation step is about 2 cm-1, comparable.
- 3R and 1T polytypes break the 2H rules (see materials.md); check stacking before applying the separation.
- Calibrate with Si (about 520 cm-1) in the same spectrum; report the laser line.
- Doping and strain both move A1': a single spectrum cannot separate all causes; say so.

## What to ask
- Laser wavelength, power at the sample, spot size, objective; was power varied?
- Substrate (SiO2 thickness), suspended or supported, encapsulated (hBN), transferred or as-grown.
- Exfoliated or CVD; age and storage; any gating or illumination history.
- Polarization configuration; temperature and environment (air, vacuum).
- Grating, resolution and calibration reference.

## Reference figures
- Lee 2010, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2a,b: spectra and E2g1/A1g positions vs layer number (514.5 nm).
- Zhang X. 2013, arXiv:1212.6796, Fig. 2: 5L, 6L, bulk spectra incl. low-frequency modes, XX vs YX.
- Zhang X. 2015, arXiv:1502.00701, Fig. 12: resonant (633 nm) spectra of 1, 2, 4, 7L and bulk.
- Conley 2013, arXiv:1305.3880, Fig. 2: E' splitting under uniaxial strain.

# Artifacts and red flags in Raman spectra of 2D materials

Each entry: what it looks like, how to tell it from a real band, what to do. Sources in brackets.

## Cosmic-ray spikes
- One to three pixels wide, far narrower than any phonon line at the instrument resolution, present in one
  acquisition only. Real lines have the instrument's minimum width and repeat across accumulations or angles.
- Remove before fitting (modified z-score on the first difference: Whitaker and Hayes, Chemom. Intell. Lab. Syst.
  179, 82, 2018). In an angle series, replace spike pixels from the most similar frame (Barton and Hennelly, Appl.
  Spectrosc. 73, 893, 2019). List them under artifacts, never under peaks.

## Silicon substrate
- First-order Si line near 520.7 cm-1 (a widely used calibration convention; check the offset of the fitted
  position and flag a calibration problem when it exceeds about 1 cm-1; 520 to 520.9 is reported in practice, Lee
  et al. 2010 and Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014). Second-order Si features near 950 and 980 cm-1 (Gillet et al.
  2017, arXiv 1708.05874, Fig. 1) and a 2TA band computed near 300 cm-1 (same paper, DFPT) can be mistaken for
  sample modes. Brillouin scattering from Si gives a line near
  4.5 cm-1 in ultra-low-frequency setups (Zhang et al., PRB 87, 115413, 2013).
- Assign these as 'Si substrate'. A strong Si line with weak sample bands suggests a thin flake.

## Calibration
- First-order wavelength calibration errors of 5 to 7 cm-1 have been reported (Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024,
  2012). Shifts of 1 to 3 cm-1 (layer number, strain, doping) are only meaningful after a calibration check.

## Background
- Broad fluorescence or photoluminescence slopes; remove with an asymmetric least-squares baseline (arPLS or
  asPLS). For broad bands (disordered carbon D and G, amorphous phases) a global baseline can eat real signal: fit
  a local linear background together with the peaks. A Breit-Wigner-Fano line shape can absorb a background slope;
  compare line shapes by BIC.

## Low-wavenumber cutoff
- Notch and edge filters block the region near the laser line (Bragg notch filters reach about 5 to 10 cm-1,
  Zhang et al. 2013). A missing shear or breathing mode below the cutoff is not evidence of absence.

## Plasma lines
- Laser plasma lines have a fixed absolute wavelength, so their Raman shift changes when the laser changes; they
  are very narrow and do not belong to the sample. Suspect them when a narrow line has no assignment.

## Laser heating
- Phonon lines soften and broaden with temperature. Graphene G shifts about -0.016 cm-1/K (Calizo et al., Nano
  Lett. 7, 2645, 2007); 1L WS2 about -0.0093 (E) and -0.0122 (A1g) cm-1/K (Huang et al., Sci. Rep. 2016);
  few-layer MoS2 about -0.013 and -0.012 cm-1/K (Sahoo et al., arXiv 1302.5865). A power series is the test.

## Substrate interference
- On SiO2/Si, absolute intensities and intensity ratios depend on oxide thickness and laser wavelength: graphene
  I(2D)/I(G) changed by almost 370 % for a 60 % change in SiO2 thickness (Yoon et al., PRB 80, 125422, 2009).
  Never read layer number from absolute intensity or from I(2D)/I(G) without the substrate stack.

## Resonance
- Near an excitonic resonance, second-order bands can exceed first-order ones. WS2 at 514 to 532 nm: 2LA(M) lies
  about 4 cm-1 below E2g and overlaps it (Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, 2013; Mitioglu et al., PRB 89,
  245442, 2014). Fit both or the E2g position and layer count are wrong.

## Saturation and clipping
- A flat-topped peak or values at the detector maximum: the peak shape and intensity are wrong; ask for a shorter
  exposure.

input.summary: Layer number from the E'/A1' separation (Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b, 514.5 nm, SiO2/Si): flake B is monolayer (Δ = 19.23 ± 0.10 cm-1), flake A is bilayer (Δ = 21.43 ± 0.08), flake D is about 4 layers (Δ = 24.27 ± 0.03, but the table has no entry between 4L and bulk, so 4 to about 6 layers cannot be excluded), and flake C is thick (Δ = 25.07 ± 0.08, essentially the bulk value 25.2): Δ saturates above about 5 layers, so C is "bulk-like, at least about 5 layers" and no exact number can be given from this spectrum. The ordering B < A < D < C is the same for Δ and for the MoS2/Si integrated-area ratio (0.24, 0.59, 1.57, 2.1), which is a supporting check only if all four were acquired under identical conditions. The fitted E'/A1' pairs are clean and stable under narrower fit windows. Caveats: the 2H vs 3R stacking is not decided by these spectra (the top library hit is 3R-MoS2), no AFM was done, and the absolute positions carry about 0.7 cm-1 of Si-calibration uncertainty, though Δ does not depend on it.

observations.finding: Flake B is monolayer by the separation relation (single candidate, 1L).
observations.evidence: rl_fit/rl_series E' 383.91 ± 0.03 cm-1 (raw), A1' 403.14 ± 0.10 cm-1; Δ = 19.23 ± 0.10 cm-1 vs table 1L Δ = 19.1; apply_relation returns 1L, confidence high, with delta_err 0.5. Narrower refit (window 340-560) gives the same positions.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b (via mos2_layer_number_from_separation)

observations.finding: Flake A is bilayer by the separation relation (single candidate, 2L).
observations.evidence: E' 383.37 ± 0.02 cm-1, A1' 404.80 ± 0.07 cm-1 (raw); Δ = 21.43 ± 0.08 cm-1 vs table 2L Δ = 21.4; apply_relation returns 2L, confidence high. The 3L value (23.1) is 1.7 cm-1 away and is excluded at delta_err 0.5.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b

observations.finding: Flake D is about 4 layers by the table, but 4 to about 6 layers cannot be excluded.
observations.evidence: E' 382.37 ± 0.01, A1' 406.64 ± 0.03 (raw); Δ = 24.27 ± 0.03 cm-1 vs table 4L Δ = 24.3 and bulk 25.2. apply_relation gives 4L with moderate confidence. The table has no 5L to 8L entries, so the mapping between 4L and bulk is not established by the tool.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b; saturation above about 5L from Zhang X. et al. 2013, PRB 87, 115413, arXiv:1212.6796 (abstract, Fig. 2)

observations.finding: Flake C is bulk-like (at least about 5 layers); the separation cannot give its exact layer number.
observations.evidence: E' 382.24 ± 0.04, A1' 407.31 ± 0.06 (raw); Δ = 25.07 ± 0.08 cm-1 vs bulk 25.2 (apply_relation: bulk, moderate). Above about 5 layers the separation saturates, so Δ cannot distinguish 6 layers from thicker flakes.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b; Zhang X. et al. 2013, PRB 87, 115413, arXiv:1212.6796 (saturation above about 5L; low-frequency shear and breathing modes needed)

observations.finding: Ordering of flakes by thickness agrees between the separation and the Si-normalized MoS2 signal.
observations.evidence: Δ: B 19.23 < A 21.43 < D 24.27 < C 25.07. Integrated E' area / Si (520) area from rl_fit: B 2134/8768 = 0.24; A 4236/7153 = 0.59; D 8407/5344 = 1.57; C 1099/519 = 2.12 (C Si fit unreliable, see below). Peak-height ratios give the same order: B 0.40, A 0.96, D 2.74, C 4.5. Valid only if integration time, power and focus were identical, which is not stated.
observations.source: Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835 (abstract): Si-normalized MoS2 signal is monotonic with N; interference-dependent intensities per MoS2 note (Buscema et al. 2014, arXiv:1311.3869)

observations.finding: Raw (uncorrected) positions of all four flakes match the Lee 2010 reference modes; the Si line shows a -0.7 cm-1 offset that would move them away from the table if applied.
observations.evidence: Si line 520.02 / 520.00 / 519.99 cm-1 in A, B, D (offset -0.68, -0.70, -0.71 vs 520.7). Raw E'/A1': A 383.37/404.80 vs 2L 383.4/404.8; B 383.91/403.14 vs 1L 384.0/403.1; C 382.24/407.31 vs bulk 382.2/407.4; D 382.37/406.64 vs 4L 382.4/406.7. Si-corrected values are 0.6 to 0.7 cm-1 above the table. Table values were read from the figure (about ±0.3 cm-1), so the raw match may be partly coincidental.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b (table read to about ±0.3 cm-1); Si reference 520.7 cm-1 from the artifacts note

observations.finding: No strain or doping signature beyond calibration is resolvable; E' positions match the table within the figure-reading uncertainty.
observations.evidence: E' offsets from table (raw): A -0.03, B -0.09, C +0.04, D -0.03 cm-1, all within ±0.3. A1' of A is 404.80 vs 2L table 404.8 (no shift). A1' FWHM of A is 6.16 ± 0.29 cm-1 (broad end of the 3 to 6 cm-1 range), but without an A1' shift this does not point to electron doping (rule of thumb in MoS2 note: A1' shift with broadening = doping).
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, text p.4 (A1g width 3 to 6 cm-1 from 6L to 2L); Conley et al. 2013, arXiv:1305.3880 (E' -4.5 cm-1/% uniaxial strain, A1' unshifted); Chakraborty et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.1758 (electron doping softens A1g)

observations.finding: E' linewidths are about 2.0 to 2.1 cm-1 in all four flakes, below the stated 2.7 cm-1 spectral resolution, so widths cannot be read as intrinsic crystal quality or defect density here.
observations.evidence: E' FWHM: A 2.12 ± 0.10, B 2.04 ± 0.09, C 2.10 ± 0.12, D 2.08 ± 0.02 cm-1 (rl_series, Lorentzian fit). Spectral resolution 2.7 cm-1 (user-stated).
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509 (Γ(E2g1) about 2.1 cm-1 at comparable resolution, text p.4); Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) near 227 as defect band; no defect claim made here)

observations.finding: The 320 and 330 cm-1 components in D are fit artifacts of a broad background, not MoS2 modes; they do not change the thickness result.
observations.evidence: rl_fit on D: components at 320.8 (FWHM 38, position error ±25) and 329.9 (FWHM 33, ±16). Residual is negative (model above data) by up to about 200 counts over 290 to 350 cm-1. Refit with window 360-560 gives E' 382.371 and A1' 406.639 (Δ 24.27, unchanged) and no 320/330 components. Library matcher leaves them unmatched. Si second-order 2TA (computed near 300 cm-1) is the other candidate, but B and A show no such feature.
observations.source: Gillet et al. 2017, arXiv:1708.05874, Fig. 1 (Si 2TA computed near 300 cm-1)

observations.finding: B's broad 222 cm-1 component is not a resolved peak; it gives no LA(M) defect evidence.
observations.evidence: B: position 222.2 ± 48.2 cm-1, FWHM 64.9 ± 210.7 cm-1, height 73 ± 495. Refit with window 340-560 leaves E'/A1' unchanged (383.905 / 403.137). LA(M) defect band would be near 227 cm-1 but needs a narrow, well-determined line.
observations.source: Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) near 227 cm-1 as defect-activated band; MoS2 note)

observations.finding: Library matcher: the top candidate is 3R-MoS2 (R3m, CRD row 98), matched only on the E/A pair; other top hits are unrelated compounds on the same two modes, so the match does not identify stacking.
observations.evidence: match_library on D peaks (383.08, 407.35, 320.8, 329.9, 519.99): R3m MoS2 score 0.76 (E 383.4, A1 406.8 matched); BrOPr 0.74, I3InO9 0.71, Cl6NaNb 0.65, Cl6NaTa 0.58 all matched on two modes with strong unmatched modes. Stacking (2H vs 3R) is not separable from E/A pair alone.
observations.source: Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80 (Computational Raman Database); MoS2 note: 2H vs 3R bilayers differ in low-frequency modes, not the E/A pair (Ranjuna et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13, 16418, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-43756-w, Fig. 1d to f)

observations.finding: Flake C has no usable Si calibration line and one cosmic-ray spike. Its Si-normalized ratio is high, which is consistent with strong MoS2 absorption attenuating the Si line in a thick flake, but this is not proof.
observations.evidence: rl_qc: no Si line flagged for C; Si fit at 519.94 ± 0.29 cm-1, FWHM 4.5, height 74 vs E' height 334 (Si about 4.5x weaker than in A/B/D relative to MoS2). Spike at 265.1 cm-1 removed (artifact). SNR 19 (warning). For C use raw positions; the --si-correct value (-0.76) is unreliable.
observations.source: Artifacts note (cosmic-ray spikes and Si substrate line, Gillet 2017, arXiv:1708.05874); Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835 (interference)

observations.finding: No second-order or defect-activated bands are resolved in any spectrum, and the laser is off the A exciton, so the spectra are E' and A1' only.
observations.evidence: Fit windows 150 to 650 cm-1 show only E', A1' and Si (plus artifacts discussed). No 2LA(M) near 450 cm-1 in any spectrum. Laser 514.5 nm (off the A exciton).
observations.source: MoS2 note: off resonance (514, 532 nm) the spectrum is mainly E' and A1' (Zhang X. et al. 2015, arXiv:1502.00701, Fig. 12, pp.13-14)

observations.finding: Modest laser heating does not change Δ meaningfully; both modes redshift together.
observations.evidence: Few-layer MoS2 coefficients: E2g -0.013, A1g -0.012 cm-1/K, so dΔ/dT about 0.001 cm-1/K; a 10 K heating shifts E' by about -0.13 cm-1 and Δ by about 0.01 cm-1. Laser power at sample is unknown.
observations.source: Sahoo et al. 2013, J. Phys. Chem. C, arXiv:1302.5865, p.6 (coefficients as recorded in relations.md)

caveats: Layer assignment uses a 285 nm SiO2 reference (Lee 2010) at 514.5 nm and 2.7 cm-1 resolution, which match the user's conditions. The table values were read from a figure (about ±0.3 cm-1 each), so Δ has about ±0.4 cm-1 systematic uncertainty. That is enough for 1L/2L/3L separation but not for 4L vs 5L.

The Lee table has entries only for 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L and bulk. The separation saturates above about 5L, so 5 to 8 layers cannot be resolved by this relation. C is reported as bulk-like and D as 4 to about 6 layers for this reason.

Stacking (2H vs 3R) is unverified. The top library hit is 3R-MoS2 (R3m), but the matcher only compares the E/A pair and cannot separate polytypes. Natural molybdenite can contain both polytypes. The distinguishing low-frequency shear and breathing modes lie below the 150 cm-1 start of the data.

Absolute positions depend on calibration. The Si line in A, B and D sits at 520.0 cm-1 (-0.7 vs 520.7). Si-correcting moves all MoS2 positions by about +0.7 cm-1; Δ is unchanged. Raw positions match the table within 0.1 cm-1, which may be coincidental given the table reading uncertainty. For C, the Si correction is not meaningful (weak Si line, position error 0.29 cm-1), so raw positions should be used.
The Si-normalized intensity ratios assume identical integration time, laser power, focus and oxide thickness across the four spectra. None of these were stated.

Fitted E' widths (about 2.1 cm-1) are narrower than the 2.7 cm-1 stated resolution. They are not interpretable as intrinsic linewidths. The A1' width of flake A (6.2 cm-1) is at the broad end of the table range but is not a shift-plus-broadening doping signature.

The D fit's 320 and 330 cm-1 components and the B fit's 222 cm-1 component were checked by refitting with narrower windows. Their positions carry errors of 16 to 211 cm-1, so they are not resolved modes. No literature search was run; the curated MoS2 note and the Lee 2010 table were used throughout.

Temperature is recorded as 295 K. The Lee 2010 table temperature is null in the tool, so the reference is assumed to be room temperature. Laser power at the sample is unknown and could heat the flakes; the heating coefficients suggest this would shift Δ by under 0.01 cm-1 per 10 K.
questions_for_user: Is AFM (or step-height) available for at least C and D? C is saturated in Δ and D's table assignment is ambiguous between 4 and 6 layers; AFM is the only independent thickness check, and the four flakes look different under the microscope.

What was the laser power at the sample, integration time, focus and number of accumulations, and were all four flakes measured under identical settings? The Si-normalized ratio ordering depends on this.

Was the spectrometer calibrated against Si on the day of measurement? The Si line at 520.0 cm-1 suggests a -0.7 cm-1 offset; a standard (e.g. Si at 520.7 or a neon line) would settle whether the absolute positions or the Si line is off.
Is the SiO2 thickness 285 nm (the stated Lee 2010 reference)? Oxide thickness changes the intensities and interference-based contrast, and the Si-ratio argument depends on it.

Do you need 2H confirmed? Natural molybdenite can contain 3R stacking. A low-frequency (shear and breathing) measurement with a notch filter reaching about 10 to 20 cm-1 would decide the stacking and extend the layer count beyond 5L, where Δ saturates.

Were any spots scanned repeatedly or at high power? Laser exposure can sublimate upper layers of multilayer MoS2 on SiO2 (Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.4323) and can change intensities (Bera et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386), so repeated scans of one spot are not independent.
What polarization geometry was used? Only the E'/A1' pair was analysed here; a polarization series would separate the two modes further and help check the irreps.

toolu_01DPFU3iRnLDVTYd4Qxohg5g.summary: Layer number from the E'/A1' separation (Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b, 514.5 nm, SiO2/Si): flake B is monolayer (Δ = 19.23 ± 0.10 cm-1), flake A is bilayer (Δ = 21.43 ± 0.08), flake D is about 4 layers (Δ = 24.27 ± 0.03, but the table has no entry between 4L and bulk, so 4 to about 6 layers cannot be excluded), and flake C is thick (Δ = 25.07 ± 0.08, essentially the bulk value 25.2): Δ saturates above about 5 layers, so C is "bulk-like, at least about 5 layers" and no exact number can be given from this spectrum. The fitted E'/A1' pairs are clean and stable under narrower fit windows. Caveats: the 2H vs 3R stacking is not decided by these spectra (the top library hit is 3R-MoS2), no AFM was done, and the absolute positions carry about 0.7 cm-1 of Si-calibration uncertainty, though Δ does not depend on it.

observations.evidence: rl_fit/rl_series E' 383.91 ± 0.03 cm-1 (raw), A1' 403.14 ± 0.10 cm-1; Δ = 19.23 ± 0.10 cm-1 vs table 1L Δ = 19.1; apply_relation returns 1L, confidence high, with delta_err 0.5. Narrower refit (window 340-560) gives the same positions.

observations.finding: Flake A is bilayer by the separation relation (single candidate, 2L).
observations.evidence: E' 383.37 ± 0.02 cm-1, A1' 404.80 ± 0.07 cm-1 (raw); Δ = 21.43 ± 0.08 cm-1 vs table 2L Δ = 21.4; apply_relation returns 2L, confidence high. The 3L value (23.1) is 1.7 cm-1 away and is excluded at delta_err 0.5.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b

observations.finding: Flake D is about 4 layers by the table, but 4 to about 6 layers cannot be excluded.
observations.evidence: E' 382.37 ± 0.01, A1' 406.64 ± 0.03 (raw); Δ = 24.27 ± 0.03 cm-1 vs table 4L Δ = 24.3 and bulk 25.2. apply_relation gives 4L with moderate confidence. The table has no 5L to 8L entries, so the mapping between 4L and bulk is not established by the tool.

observations.finding: Flake C is bulk-like (at least about 5 layers); the separation cannot give its exact layer number.
observations.evidence: E' 382.24 ± 0.04, A1' 407.31 ± 0.06 (raw); Δ = 25.07 ± 0.08 cm-1 vs bulk 25.2 (apply_relation: bulk, moderate). Above about 5 layers the separation saturates, so Δ cannot distinguish 6 layers from thicker flakes.

observations.evidence: Δ: B 19.23 < A 21.43 < D 24.27 < C 25.07. Integrated E' area / Si (520) area from rl_fit: B 2134/8768 = 0.24; A 4236/7153 = 0.59; D 8407/5344 = 1.57; C 1099/519 = 2.12 (C Si fit unreliable, see below). Peak-height ratios give the same order: B 0.40, A 0.96, D 2.74, C 4.5. Valid only if integration time, power and focus were identical, which is not stated.
observations.source: Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835 (abstract): Si-normalized MoS2 signal is monotonic with N; interference-dependent intensities per MoS2 note (Buscema et al. 2014, arXiv:1311.3869)

observations.finding: Raw (uncorrected) positions of all four flakes match the Lee 2010 reference modes; the Si line shows a -0.7 cm-1 offset that would move them away from the table if applied.
observations.evidence: Si line 520.02 / 520.00 / 519.99 cm-1 in A, B, D (offset -0.68, -0.70, -0.71 vs 520.7). Raw E'/A1': A 383.37/404.80 vs 2L 383.4/404.8; B 383.91/403.14 vs 1L 384.0/403.1; C 382.24/407.31 vs bulk 382.2/407.4; D 382.37/406.64 vs 4L 382.4/406.7. Si-corrected values are 0.6 to 0.7 cm-1 above the table. Table values were read from the figure (about ±0.3 cm-1), so the raw match may be partly coincidental.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b (table read to about ±0.3 cm-1); Si reference 520.7 cm-1 from the artifacts note

observations.finding: No strain or doping signature beyond calibration is resolvable; E' positions match the table within the figure-reading uncertainty.
observations.evidence: E' offsets from table (raw): A -0.03, B -0.09, C +0.04, D -0.03 cm-1, all within ±0.3. A1' of A is 404.80 vs 2L table 404.8 (no shift). A1' FWHM of A is 6.16 ± 0.29 cm-1 (broad end of the 3 to 6 cm-1 range), but without an A1' shift this does not point to electron doping (rule of thumb in MoS2 note: A1' shift with broadening = doping).
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, text p.4 (A1g width 3 to 6 cm-1 from 6L to 2L); Conley et al. 2013, arXiv:1305.3880 (E' -4.5 cm-1/% uniaxial strain, A1' unshifted); Chakraborty et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.1758 (electron doping softens A1g)

observations.finding: E' linewidths are about 2.0 to 2.1 cm-1 in all four flakes, below the stated 2.7 cm-1 spectral resolution, so widths cannot be read as intrinsic crystal quality or defect density here.
observations.evidence: E' FWHM: A 2.12 ± 0.10, B 2.04 ± 0.09, C 2.10 ± 0.12, D 2.08 ± 0.02 cm-1 (rl_series, Lorentzian fit). Spectral resolution 2.7 cm-1 (user-stated).
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509 (Γ(E2g1) about 2.1 cm-1 at comparable resolution, text p.4); Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) near 227 as defect band; no defect claim made here)

observations.finding: The 320 and 330 cm-1 components in D are fit artifacts of a broad background, not MoS2 modes; they do not change the thickness result.
observations.evidence: rl_fit on D: components at 320.8 (FWHM 38, position error ±25) and 329.9 (FWHM 33, ±16). Residual is negative (model above data) by up to about 200 counts over 290 to 350 cm-1. Refit with window 360-560 gives E' 382.371 and A1' 406.639 (Δ 24.27, unchanged) and no 320/330 components. Library matcher leaves them unmatched. Si second-order 2TA (computed near 300 cm-1) is the other candidate, but B and A show no such feature.
observations.source: Gillet et al. 2017, arXiv:1708.05874, Fig. 1 (Si 2TA computed near 300 cm-1)

observations.finding: B's broad 222 cm-1 component is not a resolved peak; it gives no LA(M) defect evidence.
observations.evidence: B: position 222.2 ± 48.2 cm-1, FWHM 64.9 ± 210.7 cm-1, height 73 ± 495. Refit with window 340-560 leaves E'/A1' unchanged (383.905 / 403.137). LA(M) defect band would be near 227 cm-1 but needs a narrow, well-determined line.
observations.source: Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) near 227 cm-1 as defect-activated band; MoS2 note)

observations.finding: Library matcher: the top candidate is 3R-MoS2 (R3m, CRD row 98), matched only on the E/A pair; other top hits are unrelated compounds on the same two modes, so the match does not identify stacking.
observations.evidence: match_library on D peaks (383.08, 407.35, 320.8, 329.9, 519.99): R3m MoS2 score 0.76 (E 383.4, A1 406.8 matched); BrOPr 0.74, I3InO9 0.71, Cl6NaNb 0.65, Cl6NaTa 0.58 all matched on two modes with strong unmatched modes. Stacking (2H vs 3R) is not separable from E/A pair alone.
observations.source: Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80 (Computational Raman Database); MoS2 note: 2H vs 3R bilayers differ in low-frequency modes, not the E/A pair (Ranjuna et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13, 16418, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-43756-w, Fig. 1d to f)

observations.finding: Flake C has no usable Si calibration line and one cosmic-ray spike. Its Si-normalized ratio is high, which is consistent with strong MoS2 absorption attenuating the Si line in a thick flake, but this is not proof.
observations.evidence: rl_qc: no Si line flagged for C; Si fit at 519.94 ± 0.29 cm-1, FWHM 4.5, height 74 vs E' height 334 (Si about 4.5x weaker than in A/B/D relative to MoS2). Spike at 265.1 cm-1 removed (artifact). SNR 19 (warning). For C use raw positions; the --si-correct value (-0.76) is unreliable.
observations.source: Artifacts note (cosmic-ray spikes and Si substrate line, Gillet 2017, arXiv:1708.05874); Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835 (interference)

observations.finding: No second-order or defect-activated bands are resolved in any spectrum, and the laser is off the A exciton, so the spectra are E' and A1' only.
observations.evidence: Fit windows 150 to 650 cm-1 show only E', A1' and Si (plus artifacts discussed). No 2LA(M) near 450 cm-1 in any spectrum. Laser 514.5 nm (off the A exciton).
observations.source: MoS2 note: off resonance (514, 532 nm) the spectrum is mainly E' and A1' (Zhang X. et al. 2015, arXiv:1502.00701, Fig. 12, pp.13-14)

observations.finding: Modest laser heating does not change Δ meaningfully; both modes redshift together.
observations.evidence: Few-layer MoS2 coefficients: E2g -0.013, A1g -0.012 cm-1/K, so dΔ/dT about 0.001 cm-1/K; a 10 K heating shifts E' by about -0.13 cm-1 and Δ by about 0.01 cm-1. Laser power at sample is unknown.
observations.source: Sahoo et al. 2013, J. Phys. Chem. C, arXiv:1302.5865, p.6 (coefficients as recorded in relations.md)

structured_output.summary: Layer number from the E'/A1' separation (Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b, 514.5 nm, SiO2/Si): flake B is monolayer (Δ = 19.23 ± 0.10 cm-1), flake A is bilayer (Δ = 21.43 ± 0.08), flake D is about 4 layers (Δ = 24.27 ± 0.03, but the table has no entry between 4L and bulk, so 4 to about 6 layers cannot be excluded), and flake C is thick (Δ = 25.07 ± 0.08, essentially the bulk value 25.2): Δ saturates above about 5 layers, so C is "bulk-like, at least about 5 layers" and no exact number can be given from this spectrum. The ordering B < A < D < C is the same for Δ and for the MoS2/Si integrated-area ratio (0.24, 0.59, 1.57, 2.1), which is a supporting check only if all four were acquired under identical conditions. The fitted E'/A1' pairs are clean and stable under narrower fit windows. Caveats: the 2H vs 3R stacking is not decided by these spectra (the top library hit is 3R-MoS2), no AFM was done, and the absolute positions carry about 0.7 cm-1 of Si-calibration uncertainty, though Δ does not depend on it.

caveats: Layer assignment uses a 285 nm SiO2 reference (Lee 2010) at 514.5 nm and 2.7 cm-1 resolution, which match the user's conditions. The table values were read from a figure (about ±0.3 cm-1 each), so Δ has about ±0.4 cm-1 systematic uncertainty. That is enough for 1L/2L/3L separation but not for 4L vs 5L.

The Lee table has entries only for 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L and bulk. The separation saturates above about 5L, so 5 to 8 layers cannot be resolved by this relation. C is reported as bulk-like and D as 4 to about 6 layers for this reason.

Stacking (2H vs 3R) is unverified. The top library hit is 3R-MoS2 (R3m), but the matcher only compares the E/A pair and cannot separate polytypes. Natural molybdenite can contain both polytypes. The distinguishing low-frequency shear and breathing modes lie below the 150 cm-1 start of the data.

Absolute positions depend on calibration. The Si line in A, B and D sits at 520.0 cm-1 (-0.7 vs 520.7). Si-correcting moves all MoS2 positions by about +0.7 cm-1; Δ is unchanged. Raw positions match the table within 0.1 cm-1, which may be coincidental given the table reading uncertainty. For C, the Si correction is not meaningful (weak Si line, position error 0.29 cm-1), so raw positions should be used.
The Si-normalized intensity ratios assume identical integration time, laser power, focus and oxide thickness across the four spectra. None of these were stated.

Fitted E' widths (about 2.1 cm-1) are narrower than the 2.7 cm-1 stated resolution. They are not interpretable as intrinsic linewidths. The A1' width of flake A (6.2 cm-1) is at the broad end of the table range but is not a shift-plus-broadening doping signature.

The D fit's 320 and 330 cm-1 components and the B fit's 222 cm-1 component were checked by refitting with narrower windows. Their positions carry errors of 16 to 211 cm-1, so they are not resolved modes. No literature search was run; the curated MoS2 note and the Lee 2010 table were used throughout.

Temperature is recorded as 295 K. The Lee 2010 table temperature is null in the tool, so the reference is assumed to be room temperature. Laser power at the sample is unknown and could heat the flakes; the heating coefficients suggest this would shift Δ by under 0.01 cm-1 per 10 K.
questions_for_user: Is AFM (or step-height) available for at least C and D? C is saturated in Δ and D's table assignment is ambiguous between 4 and 6 layers; AFM is the only independent thickness check, and the four flakes look different under the microscope.

What was the laser power at the sample, integration time, focus and number of accumulations, and were all four flakes measured under identical settings? The Si-normalized ratio ordering depends on this.

Was the spectrometer calibrated against Si on the day of measurement? The Si line at 520.0 cm-1 suggests a -0.7 cm-1 offset; a standard (e.g. Si at 520.7 or a neon line) would settle whether the absolute positions or the Si line is off.
Is the SiO2 thickness 285 nm (the stated Lee 2010 reference)? Oxide thickness changes the intensities and interference-based contrast, and the Si-ratio argument depends on it.

Do you need 2H confirmed? Natural molybdenite can contain 3R stacking. A low-frequency (shear and breathing) measurement with a notch filter reaching about 10 to 20 cm-1 would decide the stacking and extend the layer count beyond 5L, where Δ saturates.

Were any spots scanned repeatedly or at high power? Laser exposure can sublimate upper layers of multilayer MoS2 on SiO2 (Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.4323) and can change intensities (Bera et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386), so repeated scans of one spot are not independent.
What polarization geometry was used? Only the E'/A1' pair was analysed here; a polarization series would separate the two modes further and help check the irreps.
